skill.name: datafusion-query-advisor
skill.description: Reviews DataFusion SQL queries and DataFrame operations for optimization issues such as predicate pushdown, partition pruning, projection, joins, and execution plans.
skill.summary: Reviews DataFusion queries and DataFrame pipelines for practical performance improvements.
skill.author: EmilLindfors

content.value_statement: Slow DataFusion queries can waste compute and hide simple plan issues. This skill reviews SQL and DataFrame patterns, then suggests concrete performance improvements.
actual_capabilities: Reviews DataFusion SQL for predicate pushdown and partition pruning opportunities.
Identifies SELECT star usage and recommends narrower column projection.
Analyzes joins, aggregations, and window functions for common performance issues.
Suggests DataFusion configuration changes for parallelism, memory, and batch size.
Guides users to validate changes with EXPLAIN, logical plans, and physical plans.
Recommends streaming results instead of collecting large datasets into memory.
limitations: It does not execute queries or measure runtime performance.
It needs the user to provide queries, schemas, plans, or workload context.
Recommendations can vary by DataFusion version, storage format, and table statistics.
It cannot replace production profiling or benchmark testing.

use_cases.title: Review a slow analytics query
use_cases.description: Find missing filters, wide projections, expensive aggregations, and plan checks before running large DataFusion workloads.

use_cases.title: Improve a Rust DataFrame pipeline
use_cases.description: Check DataFrame API usage for late filtering, large collects, and avoidable memory pressure.

use_cases.title: Tune a query service
use_cases.description: Review parallelism, memory limits, batch size, and streaming choices for DataFusion-backed services.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single SQL query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this DataFusion SQL query for performance issues. Focus on predicate pushdown, partition pruning, projection, and simple rewrites.

prompt_templates.title: Review DataFrame Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of Rust DataFrame API code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this DataFusion DataFrame workflow. Identify late filters, large collect calls, missing projection, and safer streaming options.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an EXPLAIN Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis using a query plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this DataFusion EXPLAIN output. Explain whether filters, projections, partition pruning, and joins are planned efficiently.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Workload
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across queries and runtime settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this DataFusion workload and runtime configuration. Prioritize changes for memory, parallelism, batch size, joins, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A query scans all event partitions and then filters by timestamp.
output_examples.output: The review recommends adding partition column filters and keeping the timestamp filter for correctness. It also suggests confirming pruning with EXPLAIN.

output_examples.input: A DataFrame workflow collects a huge result set before processing it.
output_examples.output: The review recommends streaming batches, applying filters before execution, and selecting only needed columns to reduce memory pressure.

output_examples.input: A join-heavy report query runs slowly on fact and dimension tables.
output_examples.output: The review suggests filtering fact data early, checking join types in the physical plan, and validating whether small tables can use broadcast joins.

best_practices: Share the query, table layout, partition columns, and expected result size.
Include EXPLAIN output when asking for plan-level performance advice.
Validate each recommendation with benchmarks or production-like samples.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for tuning advice without the query or DataFrame workflow.
Do not treat suggestions as proof without EXPLAIN or runtime validation.
Do not expose sensitive production data when sample schemas and plans are enough.

faq.question: Does this skill run DataFusion queries?
faq.answer: No. It reviews provided queries, DataFrame code, and plans, then suggests changes.

faq.question: Can it read my database or object storage?
faq.answer: No. The skill only requests the context that you provide in the conversation or files.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide SQL, DataFrame code, table schema, partition layout, row counts, and EXPLAIN output.

faq.question: Does it support both SQL and DataFrame API usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SQL queries and Rust DataFrame workflows used with DataFusion.

faq.question: Will it always improve performance?
faq.answer: No. It identifies likely issues, but real gains depend on data layout, statistics, and workload behavior.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
